title: Frame-rate independent smooth damp spring
purpose: Move numbers, vectors and angles toward targets with a critically damped spring stepped by its exact solution, so motion is the same at any frame rate and never overshoots from rest, with an optional speed limit and a stateful follower. Use it for camera follow, UI motion, aim smoothing and value easing.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: No three.js needed; plain numbers and arrays in any ES2020 runtime. The demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome.

exports.name: smoothDamp
exports.signature: smoothDamp(current, target, velocity, smoothTime, dt, maxSpeed = Infinity) -> {value, velocity}
exports.summary: One exact critically damped step for a number.

exports.name: smoothDampVector
exports.signature: smoothDampVector(current, target, velocity, smoothTime, dt, maxSpeed = Infinity) -> {value, velocity}
exports.summary: The same step for arrays of equal length; maxSpeed limits the vector speed. Returns new arrays.

exports.name: smoothDampAngle
exports.signature: smoothDampAngle(current, target, velocity, smoothTime, dt, maxSpeed = Infinity) -> {value, velocity}
exports.summary: The step for an angle in radians along the shorter arc; the value is not wrapped.

exports.name: shortestAngle
exports.summary: Signed difference along the shorter arc.

exports.name: SpringFollower
exports.signature: new SpringFollower(size, options = {}); reset(value, velocity = null); update(target, dt) -> Float64Array
exports.summary: Spring state for a vector, updated in place.

options.name: smoothTime
options.meaning: Spring time scale; w = 2 / smoothTime, so the value is 59 percent of the way after one smoothTime from rest.

options.name: maxSpeed
options.meaning: Speed a far target is approached at; Infinity for no limit.

limits: A critically damped spring only: no under-damped bounce or over-damped settings. The step is exact for a target held still during the step, so a target that moves every frame is followed one frame late, as with any per-frame update. With maxSpeed the target is pulled closer before the step; from rest the motion stays under the limit only while dt is at most smoothTime / 2, and a value that already moves faster than the limit slows down over the following steps rather than at once. Angles are radians and are not wrapped on output. Numbers are float64; the demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Critically damped harmonic oscillator, exact solution x(t) = target + (y0 + (v0 + w y0) t) e^(-w t)
Steady-state target distance solved so each step covers maxSpeed * dt
